title: Evaluating AI-Assisted Bioinformatics Analyses
text:
Welcome
Evaluating AI-Assisted Bioinformatics Analyses
Scientific reasoning, reproducibility, and evidence-based feedback
A self-guided CDI practical for researchers, students, practitioners, and learners preparing for scientific AI evaluation opportunities worldwide.






Development scaffold



This package defines the learning structure, case specifications, rubric, and report templates. Case datasets, executable analysis workflows, verified outputs, and worked solutions remain to be developed and scientifically reviewed. It is not yet a finished practical.


Begin with the preface, then work through the chapters in order.

title: Preface
text:
Purpose
Learn to inspect an AI-assisted bioinformatics analysis, verify evidence, distinguish supported conclusions from errors or uncertainty, and communicate justified corrections.

title: Preface
text:
Who this is for
Researchers, postgraduate students, bioinformatics practitioners, educators, and scientific AI evaluation candidates. Participation does not assume affiliation with a particular institution, country, employer, or qualification.

title: Preface
text:
Prerequisites
You should be able to read a data table, interpret basic statistical results, describe biological replication, and read and run a short R script. Each case will introduce its domain-specific background. Learners needing preparation should first practise these skills using relevant CDI foundation guides.

title: Preface
text:
Learning outcomes

Frame an answerable scientific question.
Check data provenance, study design, and analytical assumptions.
Verify reported results using code and supplied evidence.
Assess biological claims and acknowledge uncertainty.
Produce a reproducible evaluation report with actionable feedback.

title: Preface
section: How to use the finished practical
text:
How to use the finished practical
Attempt each task before opening its worked explanation. Record your reasoning and evidence as you go. The planned sequence moves from a guided RNA-seq case to a partially guided microbiome case and an independent single-cell case.

title: Preface
text:
Access and tools
The core exercises will use supplied responses and small datasets; a paid AI account will not be required. R verification scripts will live in scripts/R/. Chapters will display code without executing it during rendering. Package versions and setup instructions will be finalized when the case workflows are implemented.

title: Preface
text:
Scope
This resource develops demonstrable skills. Completion does not guarantee recruitment, employment, project access, or income. Exercises are original teaching materials, independent of employer assessments and workshop curricula.

title: Appendix A — Templates and evaluation rubric
text: A.1 Claim labels

title: Appendix A — Templates and evaluation rubric
text:
Supported: evidence supports the claim within its stated scope.
Incorrect: evidence or a reproducible check contradicts the claim.
Unsupported: necessary evidence is absent.
Uncertain: available evidence leaves meaningful ambiguity.

title: Appendix A — Templates and evaluation rubric
text:
A.2 Review quality rubric
Score each dimension from 0 to 3. Use these scores for feedback, not as a validated certification threshold.







Dimension
What to inspect




Question and scope
Identifies the question and appropriate limits


Data and design
Checks provenance, experimental units, and assumptions


Verification
Provides traceable checks and consistent outputs


Interpretation
Connects claims to evidence and acknowledges uncertainty


Feedback
Explains consequences and gives actionable corrections


Reproducibility
Records inputs, code, environment, and outputs



0: missing or materially incorrect. 1: identifies a concern with little support. 2: mostly correct with relevant evidence but incomplete checks or explanation. 3: justified, traceable, and clear about limitations.
A total out of 18 may summarize performance, but always report dimension-level feedback. A high total cannot compensate for a major uncorrected scientific error.

title: Appendix A — Templates and evaluation rubric
text:
A.3 Issue severity
Record separately: critical (undermines the principal conclusion), major (materially changes a result or claim), minor (limited consequence), or not applicable. Justify the level in context.

title: Appendix A — Templates and evaluation rubric
text:
A.4 Templates
The project includes an evaluation report, evidence log, reproducibility checklist, and case authoring specifications.

title: Appendix B — References and further reading
text:
